context: Rewrite the three per-mode legend strings to match lightnessForCell's direction. Add a unit test asserting the legend text against the direction the function implements, so copy and math cannot diverge. No change to chartMath.ts and no change to the parity fixtures.
description:
In `times` mode the landing matrix legend reads 'Heat: darker = faster within each ranking' (MetaLeaderboard.tsx:250). The rendering does the opposite: lightnessForCell maps fastest to 95% lightness and 10x slower to 25% (chartMath.ts:199-204), so darker is SLOWER. BenchmarkIndex's legend is correct. The landing page therefore misteaches its own encoding to every first-time reader.

An earlier plan proposed inverting the heat scale to match the legend. All three reviewers rejected that: it would break Python/TypeScript parity fixtures, invert the working QueryHeatmap, and cross dark mode, reduced-colour and forced-contrast paths. The fix is the legend text, and a test that stops the two drifting again.

Also correct the speedup-mode legend: it says 'darker = closer to ranking best (>=1.00x)', but the convention caps the best at exactly 1.00x, so >= is wrong.
